paper.citation: Hayden S. Helm, Aranyak Acharyya, Brandon Duderstadt, Youngser Park, Carey E. Priebe, Statistical inference on black-box generative models in the Data Kernel Perspective Space, arXiv:2410.01106.
paper.source_version: Retained paper prose/TeX corresponding to the Helm2025 formalization.

purpose: Compare the inference-transfer theorems and Appendix assumptions with their Lean encodings and expose every additional analytic premise.

relation_definitions.exact: The source clause and Lean clause have the same mathematical content, modulo notation/encoding.
relation_definitions.equivalent_encoding: The mathematical content is equivalent, but Lean packages it in a structurally different form.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_hypothesis: Lean assumes less than the source at this clause, so the Lean theorem is stronger here.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_hypothesis: Lean assumes more than the source at this clause; this is a source-fidelity gap unless separately justified.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_conclusion: Lean proves at least the source conclusion and additionally proves a stronger conclusion.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_conclusion: Lean proves less than the source conclusion; this is a source-fidelity gap.
relation_definitions.different_quantifier_encoding: Lean makes an informal/asymptotic quantifier pattern explicit using an equivalent or stronger schedule/event formulation.
relation_definitions.derived_by_composition: No single source-shaped declaration exists, but the source clause follows from a checked composition of cited Lean declarations.
relation_definitions.source_repair: The retained source wording is inconsistent, false, or mismatched with its proof; Lean formalizes the repaired mathematical statement.
relation_definitions.proof_role_replaced: The printed proof-side lemma is not exposed literally; a different formal proof route removes or subsumes its role.
relation_definitions.missing: No Lean theorem surface was found for this source clause.
relation_definitions.supplementary: This Lean result goes beyond the printed source and is recorded for context, not source coverage.

rows.title: Fixed-n inference risk transfer
rows.source_claim: For fixed n, as DKPS estimation budgets grow, the risk of the decision function trained/evaluated on estimated perspectives converges to the risk based on true perspectives.

clauses.source_clause: n is fixed; m,r grow and risk on estimated DKPS training data converges to risk on true DKPS training data.
clauses.lean_clause: Theorem1/risk_converges_fixed_n prove the fixed-n risk convergence along an abstract estimation-budget index.
clauses.note: The budget index packages the joint m,r growth.

clauses.source_clause: Technical assumptions are Appendix Assumptions 1--4 plus aligned embedding consistency Eq. (3).
clauses.lean_clause: Lean explicitly takes AlignmentConsistency, affine-isometry invariance, continuity of the learning rule, compact-range control, and continuous loss.

clauses.source_clause: The source does not explicitly require measurability of the embedding estimator.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean requires h_meas_psi.
clauses.note: This is a standard integration/probability side condition but still an additional theorem premise.

clauses.source_clause: Assumption 3 says the image of every h is closed, bounded, complete.
clauses.lean_clause: The main theorem uses Assumption3' / compact-range encoding.
clauses.note: In the finite-dimensional Euclidean codomain this is a sufficient compactness form.

clauses.source_clause: Assumption 4 is continuity in prediction for each fixed label.
clauses.lean_clause: The main theorem uses joint ContinuousLoss.

clauses.source_clause: No bounded/compact label-support assumption is visible in the retained source theorem or Appendix assumptions.
clauses.lean_clause: Theorem1 additionally requires LabelCompactSupport.
clauses.note: This is the most significant unresolved source-vs-Lean hypothesis discrepancy in Helm2025.

clauses.source_clause: Conclusion is convergence of the two risks.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean concludes exactly the corresponding Tendsto/risk convergence.

clauses.source_clause: The paper states no boundedness or compactness condition on the labels.
clauses.lean_clause: The theorems require LossDominated -- an integrable envelope for the loss as a function of the label -- rather than compact label support.
clauses.note: Strictly weaker than the previous hypothesis, and implied by the finiteness of the risk the paper writes down.

clauses.source_clause: Theorem 1 asserts risk convergence under Assumptions 1-4 alone.
clauses.lean_clause: Not provable as stated; prob_convergence_not_enough_for_expectations gives the escaping-mass witness. The theorem carries an integrable envelope.
clauses.note: The envelope is implied by finiteness of the risk the paper writes down.

rows.review: The conclusion is source-shaped. Lean additionally requires measurable embedding estimators, uses the compact-range form of A3, and joint loss continuity; these are sufficient conditions for the paper proof. The paper-facing wrapper also requires bounded/compact label support; no matching assumption was located in the retained source.
rows.notes: The compact-label hypothesis, which no source passage states, has been replaced by the integrable-envelope hypothesis LossDominated; see gap label-compact-support.
rows.next_action: None for the assumptions; Theorem1_printed now runs on the printed readings of Assumptions 2 and 4 and does not use Assumption 3.

rows.title: Consistency transfer from true to estimated DKPS embeddings
rows.verdict: REPAIR uniform integrability; GAP consistency notion
rows.source_claim: If learning on true perspectives is consistent, learning on estimated perspectives is also consistent as n,m,r grow.

clauses.source_clause: If the true-perspective learning sequence is consistent, the estimated-perspective sequence is consistent as n,m,r->infinity.
clauses.lean_clause: Theorem2_bayes proves Bayes-risk consistency transfer.

clauses.source_clause: The source uses a three-parameter informal joint limit.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean uses a diverging diagonal budget schedule phi(n) to choose sufficiently accurate embedding stages as n grows.
clauses.note: This makes the quantifier order executable and is at least the diagonal form needed for the proof.

clauses.source_clause: Appendix Assumptions 1--4 and Eq. (3) provide the analytic transfer conditions.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean uses the same strengthened analytic forms as Theorem1 and a sequence of alignment-consistency hypotheses.

clauses.source_clause: No bounded/compact label-support premise is visible in the retained source.
clauses.lean_clause: Theorem2_bayes carries the label-support/boundedness condition used by the risk limit.

clauses.source_clause: The paper states no boundedness or compactness condition on the labels.
clauses.lean_clause: The theorems require LossDominated -- an integrable envelope for the loss as a function of the label -- rather than compact label support.
clauses.note: Strictly weaker than the previous hypothesis, and implied by the finiteness of the risk the paper writes down.

clauses.source_clause: Theorem 2 asserts the transfer under Assumptions 1-4 alone.
clauses.lean_clause: Inherits Theorem 1's repair: an integrable envelope at each sample size, with no compact-label hypothesis.

rows.review: Lean proves Bayes-risk consistency along a diverging budget schedule phi(n). The analytic hypotheses are stronger than the literal paper assumptions, and the joint (m,r) limit is represented by diagonalization. The paper-facing wrapper also requires bounded/compact label support; no matching assumption was located in the retained source.
rows.notes: The compact-label hypothesis, which no source passage states, has been replaced by the integrable-envelope hypothesis LossDominated; see gap label-compact-support.
rows.next_action: None for the assumptions; Theorem2_bayes_printed runs on the printed readings of Assumptions 2 and 4 and does not use Assumption 3.

rows.source_anchor: Appendix A.1 use of Acharyya et al. (2024) alignment consistency
rows.title: Discharge Equation (3) from an MDS consistency theorem
rows.source_claim: The proof cites the eigengap-free asymptotic raw-stress consistency theorem to obtain aligned DKPS consistency.

clauses.source_clause: The Appendix cites Acharyya 2024 raw-stress consistency to justify Eq. (3), without an eigengap premise.
clauses.lean_clause: The available end-to-end bridge realizes estimates by spectral/classical MDS and requires a positive population eigenvalue floor plus cap.
clauses.note: This discrepancy belongs to the concrete estimator bridge, not the abstract inference-transfer theorem once Eq. (3) is assumed.

clauses.source_clause: The paper route is raw-stress/affine alignment.
clauses.lean_clause: The Lean bridge is spectral/orthogonal alignment; Gram identities discharge PSD/rank, but spectral stability remains.
clauses.note: A raw-stress bridge using Acharyya2024 would be closer to the paper route.

clauses.source_clause: The cited MDS consistency theorem is eigengap-free.
clauses.lean_clause: alignmentConsistency_of_pairwiseDist has no spectral hypothesis: it derives Equation (3) from convergence in probability of the pairwise distances alone.
clauses.note: The population eigenvalue floor the spectral bridges carry is Acharyya 2025's Assumption 2 and appears nowhere in Helm; it is now removed rather than merely disclosed.

rows.review: The available end-to-end bridge realizes the estimator as spectral/classical MDS and therefore assumes a positive population eigenvalue floor. That is stronger than the Helm paper route through raw-stress consistency.
rows.notes: This discrepancy belongs to the bridge, not the abstract Theorem1/Theorem2 transfer once Equation (3) is assumed.
rows.next_action: Fiber Acharyya2024.rawStress_mds_stability_set over the latent sample to discharge the distance-convergence hypothesis.

rows.source_anchor: Statistical learning problem and Bayes risk
rows.title: Risk, the Bayes decision function, and the Bayes risk
rows.source_claim: h* in argmin_{h in H} R_l(P_fY, h), and R*_l(P_fY, H) = R_l(P_fY, h*) is the risk of h*.

clauses.source_clause: h* in argmin_{h in H} R_l(P_fY, h); R*_l(P_fY, H) = R_l(P_fY, h*).
clauses.lean_clause: bayesRisk is sInf of risk_df over the hypothesis class.
clauses.note: The infimum form does not presume the argmin is attained.

rows.review: risk_df is the expected loss of a decision function and bayesRisk is the infimum of that over the hypothesis class, which is the displayed R*_l stated as an infimum rather than as the value at a minimiser. Lean does not assume the minimiser exists, which is weaker than the paper's argmin and therefore safe.
rows.notes: The paper's argmin presumes attainment; the sInf form does not.

clauses.source_clause: Consistency is convergence in probability of the risk of the trained rule.
clauses.lean_clause: ConsistentInProbability over riskGivenTraining is that definition verbatim; it implies convergence of the averaged conditional risk under uniform absolute continuity.

See gap consistency-in-probability-vs-expectation.
rows.notes: This is the definition Theorem 2 quantifies over, so the substitution propagates to it.
